newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy well on course towards EMU goals - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy well on course towards EMU goals - Prodi.

text.p: Italy has made huge strides towards satisfying criteria for the European single currency, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday.
He said he had been particularly satisfied to have been able to tell this to leaders of mainly Christian Democrat parties at a meeting in Strasbourg earlier this week.

"At this meeting with European party leaders," Prodi said, "I told them: you haven't understood anything. For a year I've been running a government with a Reuter screen for the markets on my right and Bertinotti on my left, and everything's fine."

Prodi was referring to Fausto Bertinotti, leader of the hard-left Communist Refoundation which fiercely opposes Prodi's attempts to cut back on social spending. The party lies outside the centre-left government but guarantees its majority in the lower house of parliament.
"We said without being arrogant that we would qualify for the single currency and here we are with the numbers practically in place, and this has surprised many," Prodi told reporters.
He was speaking before a convention on public finances.

Prodi noted the Italian Btp government bond future was trading above 131.00 which he said "is a magic number." He did not elaborate. The September Btp contract was firm and well above the 131.00 level on Thursday boosted by what traders said was renewed confidence in economic and monetary union.
